# Native Desktop Presentations

This macOS Node-API v8 binding is a remote CoreAnimation consumer for an existing AppKit desktop host. Importing it does not create an application, start a run loop, or open a window. The desktop main process owns its lifetime; renderers must never receive a native handle or host token.

Production packages include this independent prebuilt component under `prebuilt/darwin-ARCH/desktop-presentations.node` with `desktop-presentations.json`. Installation and presentation startup never compile it or require Xcode. The loader checks the actual binary SHA-256, Mach-O architecture, Node-API v8 support, macOS 14 minimum, pinned official Electron version, and a valid code signature. An ad-hoc signature is supported; no matching Electron signing team or paid signing identity is required.

Maintainers build the addon with `node native/desktop-presentations/build.mjs`. The build uses the current Node installation's stable Node-API headers; `--node-include PATH` selects another installed header directory. Default output is the matching `prebuilt/darwin-ARCH` package directory. `--arch arm64|x64` selects the target and `--destination ABSOLUTE_PATH` selects a staging directory. The build applies an ad-hoc signature only to the newly built addon, or `--sign IDENTITY` selects a distributor identity, then seals the resulting bytes. After external signing, rerun `node native/desktop-presentations/seal.mjs --root ABSOLUTE_PATH --arch ARCH`. No Electron binary is modified, compiled or resigned. The schema 2 manifest contains an official runtime version contract and the addon's independent Node-API contract, with no custom engine source identity.

## Plugin Companion

The plugin now owns its AppKit presentation process. `src/computer-use/plugin-native-presentations-provider.mjs` exposes `PluginNativePresentationsProvider({directory})` with `{version:1, epoch, start, request, subscribe, waitForRelease, close}`. It resolves the plugin's pinned official Electron through `getPluginRuntimeExecutable()` and launches the fixed `plugin-native-presentations-process.mjs` main entry. Neither DSH's executable nor a custom Electron build is required. Missing runtime files produce the explicit `npm run prepare:runtime` diagnostic; the provider never downloads a runtime during a presentation request.

Each provider has an immutable epoch and a private inherited FD 3 socket. Bounded JSON requests are correlated, cancellable, and never replayed. Addon host tokens, `NSWindow`/`NSView` handles and Mach send rights stay in the actual owning main process or native channel. Its data directory is an instance-specific child of the manager's supplied absolute directory and is removed only after OS-observed child exit. Optional capability failures do not create a window. BrowserWindow is created only when an available native host is requested and owns a transparent, nonfocusable, input-passthrough companion window. The native panels, Mach producer reservations, remote contexts, real fence operations and encoded-frame relay remain the existing source-backed implementation.

```js
const service = new PluginNativePresentationsProvider({ directory: nativePresentationDataDir });
await service.start();
const consumer = new DesktopNativePresentations({ service, native, nativeViews });
await consumer.start();
const owner = await service.request('nativePresentation.owner', {});
await consumer.configureHost({ host: owner.host, layout: { ...owner.layout, activeThreadID } });
// Manager disposal retires capture/producers first, then destroys the AppKit provider.
await consumer.close();
await service.close();
```

`nativePresentation.owner` returns actual `ownerKind:'plugin-companion'`, immutable `ownerID`, `hostID:'opencu-native-floating'`, `ownerWindowID` from `NSWindow.windowNumber`, main-issued `senderID/senderGeneration`, Electron logical-point `bounds`, and actual `contentSize`. Its `host` field contains the native registration input with six Cocoa bottom-left content-space anchors, actual content rectangles, `presentationScope:0`, and `codexHomeAvailable:false`. Its `layout` contains complete initial native inputs: nullable active thread, companion host ID, alignment 1, pinned placement 1, scope 0, visible item limit 5, maximum display size 200, zero initial stack size and false handoff/home flags. A client may supply the current thread, visibility and actual video size while retaining real owner geometry. `nativePresentation.configureOwner` accepts the matching `ownerID` and integral `{x,y,width,height}` bounds; it moves this process's real window and returns freshly measured owner inputs.

`registerNativeHost` requires the matching companion `ownerKind`, `ownerID`, host ID and current measured rects/anchors. It rejects DSH handles, `codex-main-thread` registration and native home availability. This establishes the independent native floating preview and video path. It does not claim to embed a foreign DSH AppKit window. The separately registered DSH DOM video home below performs the actual video/native visibility handoff while keeping the native owner and anchor identities intact.

## DOM Video Home Handoff

The original `RemoteHostedPIPContentService.shouldHideNativeStackForDOMVideo` (`sky.node` 0x14c70) requires a current thread, nonempty actual presentation order, no failed DOM video, scope 0, logical home placement/availability and the logical main-thread target. A pending handoff additionally requires no native motion and actual DOM video readiness. `setNativeVideoReady:forThreadID:` (0x14b9c) removes the failure flag only after real readiness and resumes a DOM-suspended native move on removal. `PIPStackWindow.setHiddenForDOMVideo:` (0x31b38) affects its own panels and clears its weak physical owner; it does not take or synthesize a DOM or foreign NSWindow handle. The existing assembly/pseudocode evidence is under local `work/rea-backend/native-preview/deep/addon-assembly` and `ghidra-addon-verified`, plus the read-only native-window reconstruction tree.

The plugin maps the logical DOM-home authority to actual mounted DSH surfaces instead of a fictitious registered native main window. Its cross-process handoff starts pending and always waits for actual ready video and native motion settlement. The trusted consumer validates every requested presentation ID against its own live records and current thread; the native owner separately compares readiness against its current visible publication order. The owner window, real host ID, `nativePresentationLayout`, native scope and native anchors remain unchanged.

Manager input is `{action:'dom-home',domHome:{surfaceID,revision,available,visible,active,ready,orderedPresentationIDs}}`; the session supplies the real thread ID. `DesktopNativePresentations.configureDOMHome(threadID,domHome)` dispatches private `setDOMVideoHome`. Each actual DOM surface has its own UUID and increasing revision; native window IDs never substitute for surface identity. A ready input requires an active visible available surface, actual enabled video, and at most five distinct consumer-owned presentation IDs in the current native order. Stale revisions are declined without changing another surface. Unmount clears that surface with all flags false and an empty ID list.

The native layer records multiple surfaces separately. For the active thread in scope 0, any genuinely available, visible, active, ready surface with the exact current IDs can hide the real native panels after motion settles. A false/hidden/unmounted surface cannot clear another ready surface. If no eligible DOM surface remains, `setWindowHiddenForDOMVideo:false` reattaches and shows the same actual companion native owner; producer contexts and capture are preserved. An empty native registry remains ordered out. Legacy per-thread video-ready callbacks retain their original branch and do not impersonate the independently confirmed DOM surfaces.

`domHomeStateChanged` publishes actual native-applied state after visibility/layout work. Consumer `snapshot.domHome` contains `{threadID,ownerKind:'dsh-dom',placement:'home',available,visible,active,ready,windowHiddenForDOMVideo,surfaces}`. DOM `available` is independent of video readiness so the frontend can mount and decode the initial stream. This is a DOM role, not a replacement for `nativePresentationLayout.placement` or an assertion that a DSH NSWindow is registered. Real visual/capture/decoder handoff verification remains an integration responsibility.

`close` waits for native detachment/host terminal delivery and OS-observed process exit. `waitForRelease` is observational and resolves only for this epoch's actual destruction. Its proof distinguishes `kind:'process-exit'` with the actual child PID/exit status from `kind:'not-started'` when no native process was created. A lost socket, timeout, transport EOF or arbitrary close acknowledgment never certifies destruction of a live process. Individual `surfaceDetached` state only comes from the native event or channel snapshot; a process destruction proof is a separate cleanup path. Retry retains incomplete cleanup. The runtime migration, addon package, native popup, real Mach capture, encoded video, controls, motion and full lifecycle execution require current integrated verification; earlier source/build results do not certify a new package.

```js
const addon = loadDesktopPresentations();
const capabilities = addon.getCapabilities();
const host = addon.createHost({
  ownerWindowHandle: browserWindow.getNativeWindowHandle(),
  senderID: browserWindow.webContents.id,
  senderGeneration,
}, event => consumeNativeEvent(event));

const senderContext = { senderID, senderGeneration, hostToken: host.hostToken };
const command = (operation, payload) => host.command({ senderContext, operation, payload });
```

`createHost` requires the existing application's AppKit main thread. It compares handle bytes against live AppKit windows and their view trees without dereferencing the supplied address. Each command checks the bound sender ID, sender generation, host token, and owner window. The desktop IPC layer must additionally validate the actual sender and invalidate the host on navigation or process loss. `host.close()` is the trusted main-process disposer; owner window closure also disposes the host. A closed host cannot be reused.

## Operations

`publishRemotePresentation` creates one new item from the producer's original `presentationID`, `threadID`, `turnID`, positive uint32 `contextID`, positive uint32 `sourceGeneration`, positive finite `sourceSize: {width,height}`, boolean `contributesToStackLayout`, and `source: {targetId,viewId,pid,windowId,processIdentity,...}`. Context IDs must come from a real producer `CAContext`; capture IDs and window IDs are not context IDs. Geometry is logical points, not capture pixels. Source identifiers are the actual OpenCU selection. An existing presentation ID is rejected for every source generation, matching `publishPresentationWithID:threadID:turnID:contextID:size:` (0x18850, duplicate check 0x18938). A terminated ID is also permanently rejected within this host; its original identity/context/generation is retained in a terminal record. Invalidated thread/turn pairs reject late publication. Publication clears the same thread's completed items and appends once to native order; repeat publication cannot update metadata, size, or context. Coordinated resize/context replacement uses the private real-fence interface below. Capture metadata refresh remains with the broker.

`configureLayout` requires nullable `activeThreadID/currentHostID`, numeric `currentAlignment` (0..5), `codexPlacement`, `presentationScope`, `visibleStackItemLimit`, `maxDisplaySize`, nonnegative `stackDisplayWidth/Height`, and booleans `homeHandoffPending/codexHomeAvailable`. The published service host ID is separate from the stack window's actual owner/host ID. Home availability is derived from the valid registered `codex-main-thread` host, and moving state is derived from the native controller, not asserted by the caller. Spatial anchors and envelopes come from actual native owner/view geometry; capture bounds, caller screen rectangles, screenshot pixels, CSS coordinates, JPEG lists, and array indices do not replace it. Optional host-supplied localized strings are `hideControlTitle`, `hideForTaskMenuTitle`, `hideForAllActiveTasksMenuTitle`, `placementControlToolTip`, and `closeControlToolTip`. A missing menu localization emits a request instead of inventing UI text.

`registerNativeHost` requires `hostID`, a private main-owned `ownerWindowHandle` Buffer, `anchorContentRect:{x,y,width,height}`, `interactionPassthroughContentRect`, `anchors:[{contentPoint:{x,y},alignment}]`, `presentationScope`, and `codexHomeAvailable`. Optional `animated` and `springParameters:{damping,mass,stiffness}` preserve native host-change motion. Coordinates are owner-content-view local and convert through its actual NSView/NSWindow. `unregisterNativeHost` takes `hostID`; an existing motion target/owner remains valid until deferred source host layout runs.

`moveStackToHost` takes a real registered `hostID` and optional alignment. `{accepted:true}` means the curve was initiated, not that its host/DOM handoff or springs completed. `setPreferredAnchorAlignment` takes an alignment or null. `setMaxDisplaySize` takes `maxDisplaySize/animated`; finite native size clamps to 1..400 points, snaps to backing scale, and changes only at a 0.5-point threshold. Direct mouse resizing has a 100-point lower bound. `requestPlacement` takes exactly `home` or `pet`; unavailable actual hosts produce a pending request, never a fabricated owner. `interactWithPresentation` takes `threadID/presentationID/isLead` and preserves separate controller lead and registry publication order.

`setNativeVideoEnabled` accepts `threadID`, `enabled`, and `producerAcknowledged`. Only an already acknowledged producer state is mirrored. This binding does not enable an encoder or produce video; its `producerVideoControl` and `encodedVideo` capabilities remain false. `setNativeVideoReady` accepts `threadID/ready` only for an enabled thread and applies the recovered native/DOM hiding predicate. The caller must use actual native video readiness.

`completeThread` accepts `threadID`, marks each unfinished item complete once, runs native completion layers, and schedules its 30-second expiry on the AppKit main queue. The callback checks the exact current item and completed flag before removal. Application icons come only from the real process bundle URL through NSWorkspace; nil is valid and uses the full checkmark path. `invalidateTurn` accepts `threadID/turnID` and immediately detaches only matching active or exiting items. `removePresentation` requires `presentationID/threadID/turnID/contextID/sourceGeneration`; stale generations and identities return `{accepted:false}`. Ordinary removal transfers the item to a separate exiting motion group, runs native appearance exit animation when visible, and completes once through its animation callback or two-second fallback. Host close and turn invalidation bypass that animation.

Every event contains `{type,hostToken,senderID,senderGeneration,payload}`. Lifecycle events include `presentationPublished`, `presentationCompleted`, `presentationRemoved`, `layout`, `nativeVideoEnabledChanged`, and `hostClosed`. `presentationRemoved` is sent after the position layer and actual attachment are detached and the CoreAnimation transaction is flushed, with `surfaceDetached:true` and the original source generation/context. The synchronous removal response acknowledges the command; the event is the surface completion signal. It does not certify producer shutdown. The bridge must join this signal to the same producer connection before notifying `didEndStream`. Callback exceptions are contained. Asynchronous environment cleanup stops event delivery first and remains pending until the AppKit queue has released native resources.

Interaction also emits actual click, visibility, placement/host, DOM-video, and producer-size requests for the trusted bridge to execute. Emitting a request does not certify that external action completed. Normal close queues terminal removals and `hostClosed`, then normally releases/drains its TSFN to break the callback/binding reference cycle. Environment cleanup retains abort semantics. Display-link motion and contrast sampling stop before native link release.

Private main-process producer-channel operations include `openProducerChannel`, `cancelProducerChannel`, `forgetProducerChannel`, and `retireExitedProducerChannel`. Retirement takes the complete immutable `identity` used to open that channel and returns its actual snapshot. It requires identity-pinned kernel producer-exit evidence and never substitutes a host-release confirmation for native surface-detachment proof.

## Private Fenced Operations

`host-operations.h` declares the private Objective-C protocol `OCUNativePresentationOperations`:

```objc
- (NSDictionary *)prepareNativeOperation:(NSDictionary *)payload
                              sendRight:(CUMachSendRight *)sendRight;
- (NSDictionary *)completeNativeOperation:(NSDictionary *)payload;
```

An authenticated native receiver supplies a real CUMachSendRight object. Its port is borrowed and the wrapper stays strongly alive through the synchronous AppKit operation. These methods do not invalidate the borrowed wrapper, accept JSON port numbers, or appear as `host.command` operations.

Prepare fields are `presentationID/threadID/turnID/sourceGeneration/source` plus `operationID/kind/expectedContextID/contextID/width/height`. Identity must equal the original publication. IDs are positive exact JSON integers, equal `lastCompletedOperationID + 1`, and cannot overlap pending work. Kinds are exactly `resize`, `resize-in-progress`, and `replace-context`. Resize uses the current context; replacement uses a different context while preserving the producer source generation.

In-progress resize only sets the actual CA fence and updates the controller source-aspect target, not registry context/size. Other prepares set the fence before beginning the transaction, preserve attachment origin, store the new display-point base, append a replacement host before detaching the old one, apply identity scaling, commit, and flush. Only actual source-size application stops resize preview, not position-spring settlement. Successful prepare records pending after native work; complete checks current context/pending ID before advancing completed ID. The carrier, immutable connection identity, replies, and two-stage stream ending remain trusted main-process responsibilities. Internal prepare implementation alone does not establish a connected authenticated channel; query capabilities and preserve unavailable states.

## Recovered Scope

The source is the same `sky.node` SHA256 `1b6f1e01c220b68badeb8485e0e8c9aafb017143b3398b0886994e992226024d`. Static evidence is in the local `work/rea-reconstruction/native-window/functions` artifact and backend `work/rea-backend/native-preview/deep` artifact; those work artifacts are not required at runtime.

The two transparent panels follow `CreateStackPanel` (0x31714): 1x1 initial frame, style mask 0x80, collection behavior 0x108, level 0, no opaque background or window shadow, no hiding on deactivate, and no window-background dragging. Envelope updates follow `setEnvelopeScreenFrame` (0x3192c); owner attachment and level follow `attachToHost` (0x32578). Native anchor selection, springs, curves, drag/resize, hover, controls/fog and window-server contrast sampling are connected to real NSPanels and CVDisplayLink host-clock timestamps. Content passthrough is checked before resize, presentation, and control hit tests.

The remote attachment reproduces the guarded `CAContext/CALayerHost` intermediary from `initWithParentLayer:frame:` (0x4ac0), producer context attachment (0x4e10), scaling modes 0/1/2 (0x528c/0x52c4), real fenced prepare (0x4f14/0x50b0), and detach (0x55a8). It uses real producer contexts, not bitmap or HTML replacement. Stored scaling base size is the negotiated display-point size, never raw CVPixelBuffer dimensions; producer root geometry must agree with steady mode 0's identity transform.

Items retain position -> appearance -> shadow -> clipped remote-content layers (0x2db20). Alignment anchors are applied to appearance while preserving its frame (0x2e684); spring/blur appearance and home shadow opacity do not move the remote-content coordinate system. Completion remains a child of the clipped content layer.

Item display size follows 0x2e01c, including upscaling into a 1..400-point maximum. Rest offsets follow 0x22c68: the index increases when an item and its native attachment/motion entry both exist, independently of contributions. Visibility follows the raw presentation index compared with the supplied limit (0x1f420); contributions do not extend visibility. Ordered IDs include only the active thread's live remote presentations in native publication order (0x1427c). The eight-field layout snapshot follows 0x7cf0/0x146f8 and uses this native host's revision counter. It is not the original Codex application's revision.

The source controller's independent animated exiting-item motion group is connected to frame/envelope calculation and display-link stepping. Ordinary removal acceptance precedes its actual detach event; the latter additionally flushes CoreAnimation before asserting surface detachment. Software cursor, producer capture/encoded video, and external callback workflows are separate capabilities. The authenticated Mach carrier is our transport, not a claim to implement the original XPC ABI. Compilation and non-UI loading are build checks, not native visual/lifecycle parity; no product UI, display-link execution, deployment, or test matrix has been performed.

The private `retireExitedProducerChannel` command addresses only an existing immutable producer identity. Its native adapter uses a pre-registered, audit-identity-bound kernel process-exit monitor before initiating source-failure removal. Transport EOF and timeouts are not exit proof. The command may return a pending snapshot; only actual surface detach and carrier close complete retirement. An unused reservation can be cancelled separately. This is OpenCU provider failure recovery, not an assertion about Codex's original XPC implementation.
